evidence: Source reading, source repo `1f2d5dd` (branch `backend-pagasa-privacy`) and Space `8ffbbb5`.

claim: Neither the deployed app nor the batch predictor applies X1 or the 0.601 threshold; both exist only in the historical scoring script `_w1_recall_floor.py`.
evidence: Source reading; `THRESHOLD_CONFIG.md` ("the X1/threshold-0.601 scoring logic exists only in experiments/w1x1/_w1_recall_floor.py").

claim: W1 trained on primary-station rows dated before 2020-10-15 **plus** all Port Area rows (to 2023-10-30) **plus** all 69,388 supplementary rows (to 2024-12-30), in one `model.fit` call. There is no pre-training/fine-tuning stage.
Early stopping was configured on the three primary stations, 2020-10-15 to 2021-10-14 (`val_gale_prob_loss`, patience 12, best weights restored).

No training history, training log or random seed for W1 exists. The stopping epoch ("stopped at epoch 49, best epoch 37") is stated only in `THRESHOLD_CONFIG.md`. The committed `dataset_audit.log` belongs to an earlier run (its counts do not match W1's split).
evidence: `_train_w3.py` never saves `history`; Stage 2 counts vs `dataset_audit.log`.

claim: W1+X1's originally declared rule (max-F1 on TUNE) selected 0.62 and was scored on TEST (TP 20, FP 7). The 0.601 'recall-floor' rules were introduced afterwards; every threshold from 0.601 to 0.627 gives the identical TUNE matrix, so 0.601 vs 0.62 is decided only by tie-breaking direction.
evidence: `variant_score_w3_x1.json`; `_w1_recall_floor.py` lines 1026-1159; Cohort A run a-legacy-20261023T162426Z-b5f446.

claim: X1 (same-day mean across stations) was carried forward after it 'had the best TEST PR-AUC in the previous scan'.
